label: copy phase: fed-back x as the first copied token (step after <DEL>)
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase when the input token is x, i.e. the model own echoed output x is fed back. Strongest and most reliable at the step right after the first copy output (recall_idx 1, prev input <DEL>, so the original sequence began with x): 91% of activation mass, 95% precision. Weaker, less reliable tail when x is fed back at recall_idx 2-3 (about 9% of mass); essentially never at recall_idx >= 4. Magnitude is larger for short sequences (L 4-5) and top examples begin x x. Does not fire on x in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other copy-phase input token.

issues: Most of the stated facts check out on test: all activation mass is in the copy phase, in_tok x accounts for ~100% of mass, recall_idx 1 holds 91% of mass, and the feature never fires at recall_idx >= 4. The predicate's test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.949, R 0.692, F1 0.800, mass recall 0.910).

Systematic miss: the 'weaker, less reliable tail' at recall_idx 2 is reliable for short sequences. On test, (in_tok==x)&(recall_idx==2)&(L<=5) has precision 0.76 and covers 19% of all active steps. Over all lengths, recall_idx 2 has precision only 0.36. So the 'widening drops precision to 0.65' result comes from recall_idx 2 at long L, not from recall_idx 2 being unreliable in general. The weak tail depends on length, and the explanation does not say so.

Systematic false positives: the predicate's inactive cases are concentrated at L=9 (step 10). In test misses, every shown false positive is x at recall_idx 1 with L=9. On its own, recall_idx==1 & L==9 has precision 0.72, versus about 0.95 overall. The feature cuts off by absolute step (nothing beyond t=12), which fits the length dependence.
The label 'first copied token' overclaims. It ignores that about 31% of active steps (count recall) are x fed back at recall_idx 2-3, which are mostly short sequences.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: x, h, l, y, 1, v; least: 3, b, f, o) and the token being output (most: x, h, 1, m, l, y; least: u, p, 2, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, t=7, t=6.
